text.text_excerpt: Looking for something different & cultural to do in New Orleans. We weren't sure what to expect when we signed up last minute for this class on our last day. Turned out to be one of our best experiences in NOLA. First off, it was more like demonstration class than a "hands on" cooking class. We sat in large round table with 8 others and watched the chef cook chicken and andouille sausage gumbo, creole chicken and pralines. Our chef du jour, Pat, was like a funnier and lively version of Paula Deen, effortlessly feeding us entertaining history of New Orleans while whipping up a masterpiece. Was slightly disappointed that she didn't cook the Jumbalaya when it was on the menu for that day. Po...

We had a great time celebrating our visit to New Orleans and trying some authentic dishes! Our Chef was amazing and very informative about the food he made for us. The staff was super friendly and made sure we had all we needed. I'm also glad he made enough for seconds because everything tasted so good. We want to come back to the class where you cook food on your own and give it a try. In the meantime, I will hopefully use the information and recipes to make it at home. Thank you for a great time!

The cooking class at the New Orleans School of Cooking was something of a last minute choice. We had a flight back to CA at 3pm on Saturday and on Friday evening we called and reserved two spots for the 10am class the next day. So simple. We strolled over to the school, just a couple blocks of Bourbon St., and made our way into a small room of tables with a kitchen/stage in the front. For the next two and a half hours, we got cooking instructions for gumbo, jambalaya, pralines, and bread pudding. What I liked best was the history of the food and local culture.
